facts.research_assertion: The study synthesized an NCBI-derived SYK-6 ligA-ligB cluster rather than acquiring genomic DNA. The insert gained upstream NdeI and downstream additional stops/BamHI; DNA2.0 supplied pJ241, then pET15b was used. BL21 E. coli expressed alpha-N-terminal His-tagged / beta-untagged material. No complete synthesized insert or residual scar sequence is supplied.

Aerobic purification used Ni-NTA; anaerobic purification used nitrogen (<5 ppm O2), Ni-NTA, bovine thrombin 1 U/mg to remove the His tag, then Source-Q. Final storage contained 0.5 mM DTT and 0.5 mM ferrous ammonium sulfate. The methods do not explicitly cleave the tag in the aerobic branch.

Before assays the enzyme was exchanged into degassed 50 mM Tris pH7.5 /10% t-butanol under nitrogen; O2 consumption was read by a Clark electrode. Organic-substrate kinetics used 1–5000 micromolar substrate and 3–7 nM LigAB. O2 kinetics used 1 mM PCA and 40–450 micromolar O2.

Gallate: apparent Km441±55 micromolar, kcat53±2 s−1, efficiency1.21e5 M−1s−1; air-saturated buffer, pH7.5,25C. This demonstrates gallate-dependent O2 turnover, not direct chemical identification of the gallate product.
facts.disposition: supplement existing gallate catalysis evidence; do not alone establish formal product

Substrate screening used5mM compound,3–350nM enzyme,25C and air-saturated50mM Tris pH7.5. Poor-substrate assays corrected dilution by the anaerobic-enzyme solution. Solvent differed among stock solutions, including10% or20%DMSO stocks. Negative results are conditional, not universal inability.

Seven substrates: PCA100%,gallate24%,3OMG3%,DHBAm33%,HPCA0.2%,catechol0.17%,3,4-dihydroxybenzonitrile0.04%, each relative to5mM PCA. The SI catechol drawing also prints an unexplained17.2% after0.17%; do not replace the table value with17.2.

Black-coded compounds (conditional no substrate/no inhibition): vanillic acid,vanillin,methyl3,4-dihydroxybenzoate,3,4-dihydroxybenzaldehyde,syringic acid,2-methoxy-4-methylphenol,3,4-dimethoxybenzaldehyde,syringaldehyde,1,2-dihydroxy-4-aminobenzene,ethylvanillin,4-hydroxybenzoic acid,3-methoxyphenol,benzoic acid,2-iodobenzoic acid,veratrole,2-aminophenol,caffeic acid,p-coumaric acid. Later2015SI reports small inhibition for five of these and activation for three; preserve both source-specific observations.

After1h EDTA LigAB retained65% PCA activity atpH7.5; after24h with1or2mM EDTA it retained35%. The short-treatment concentration is not explicitly given in the result sentence. Separately1mM EDTA2h gave50%, used in Cu challenge. Do not apply the latter dose automatically to the1h measurement.

2mM2,2′-bipyridine at4C underN2 gave50% PCA activity after1h and complete loss after24h; readout250micromolarPCA in50mMTrispH7.5. This harsh stripping protocol does not prove reversible physiological regulation.

Bipyridine-stripped enzyme after24h recovered only5% untreated PCA activity with2mMFeSO4 for1h anaerobically at4C; longer Fe incubation did not improve recovery. This is partial rescue of pretreated enzyme, not a5% native iron cofactor occupancy.

Under the same stripping/reconstitution protocol, Cu,Co,Mn,Mg,Ni,Zn divalent sulfate salts did not rescue PCA activity. This does not establish that all alternative metals inhibit active LigAB, or that metal substitution can never work.

Partially active material generated by1mM EDTA2h retained50%; subsequent2mMCu2+1h reduced residual PCA activity to8% of untreated. Co2+ andMn2+ did not produce the same additional loss on the partially active preparation. Competitive displacement ofFe is an interpretation, not a direct binding measurement.

Anaerobic preparations showed>10fold activity over aerobic preparations in PCA assays. Aerobic material lost~20%activity/hour after thaw; DTT/ascorbate did not rescue or enhance it (doses unstated). Anaerobic frozen material showed no loss over6months at−80C. Purification/tag differences co-vary, so do not attribute the entire contrast solely to oxygen.

PCA rate peaked nearpH7.5 inphosphate; phosphate rates were~20%higher thanTris. Fitted acidicpKa~6.3 andbasic~9.7; assignment to particular catalytic residues orTris competition remains proposed. Methods say23C while figure conditions state25C.

Table3Fe/LigAB ratios:desalted4.4,pH6 zero,pH7.5 0.2,pH10 1.04. The total-iron assay followedambient buffer exchange. Do not call these native binding stoichiometries or directFeII/FeIII measurements; storage/excess iron was present before exchange.

Prose first calls the acidic samplepH6.5 versusTable3/methodspH6; laterpH7.5 ratio1:4 versusTable3.2(1:5). Preserve exact table values. FeIII predominance atpH10, differential affinity,andKd are interpretations; noLigABKd was measured.

Product identification was performed on PCA, not gallate. UV/NMR and conversion to2,4-lutidinic acid support4,5-cleavage/CHMS. DirectCHMSNMRpeaks were unresolved due to equilibrium; derivativeNMR supportsassignment. No primary gallate-product stereochemistry follows from these experiments.
The Figure4 caption calls acidpH2 whereas the actual legend andmethods/text usepH1. The plots were visually read; retain the discrepancy.

Calculated oxidation potentials and PDB1B4U active-site comparisons offer electronic/steric hypotheses. Phe103alpha,His12/61/127/195beta,Glu242beta,Ser269beta,Asn270beta,Thr271beta assignments are structure-based interpretation here, not new mutagenesis or direct inhibitor-binding experiments.
facts.disposition: mechanistic hypotheses; no causal residue edges

facts.research_assertion: The discussion calls inhibitors competitive, but the inspected single-concentration inhibition protocol does not establish a full competitive-inhibition kinetic model. Preserve observed inhibition without claiming a measuredKi or proven binding mode.

FeII oxidation/superoxide release is a proposed explanation of turnover inactivation drawing on other enzymes; the2013study did not directly measure superoxide release or site-specific Fe oxidation during gallate turnover.

The comparative enzyme table lists18enzyme rows; only theLigABrow isThisWork. Other taxa/stoichiometries are historical context, including a speculativeComamonasalpha2beta2assembly. Do not transfer it to this syntheticSYK6preparation.
